albums.description: Tracklist provided by L$, without a date. If an unsourced Wikipedia claim is to be believed about Travis announcing 'Owl Pharaoh' as an 11 track EP with 2 bonus tracks, this tracklist is from late 2011. That being said, it's also possible that the Wikipedia entry was written by someone who saw this on KTT. Either way, it's the last version to use certain 2011 songs, so it was likely one of the final versions before it was reworked. ---------- Bonus ---------- The tracklist as written by L$ had the slashes between the titles in tracks 4 and 10. The titles either side of the slash for track 10 seem to suggest that they are alternate titles rather than two songs connected together, meaning that "Avenues of America" is likely to be an alternative title for "16 Chapels" and not its own song.

albums.name: Owl Pharaoh
albums.description: Supposed early version of the project that leaked on KTT on June 1, 2013. Pharaohxx sold it to KTT user Fitz, who leaked it. The original, unsequenced order of the files is as follows: It's unclear whether this is a genuine early version of the project or simply a collection of random demos. Pharaoxx stated that he left out the original version of "Sin City" and the version of "Gold 88" with Pusha T, which suggests that it's merely a compilation, though the inclusion of songs like "16 Chapels", "Night", and "Illamerica", which were all already released/leaked, suggest that the leak was an early version of the project, or at the very least a collection of songs that were being considered for the project. KTT user mikelangelo (who leaked the LQ version of "Sin City" and knew Travis) claimed to have heard a very similar version of the project over a phonecall with Travis. mikelangelo stated that the call took place in December 2012, so it's possible that he heard a later version; if this is the case, the songs being unfinished here makes more sense, and Pharaohxx's comment about leaving things out may have been a bluff. We know that "Gold 88" had Pusha T from July 28, 2012, at the latest, so it's possible that this is a version of the project from before he was added. There are three probable scenarios (in no particular order): 1) this is a random compilation of demos that Pharaohxx had on-hand; 2) this is a collection of songs that were being considered for the project (effectively an early version) sometime close to July 2012; or 3) this is an incomplete version of the project from December 2012 that is missing some songs and some correct versions of songs.

albums.description: A partial 'tracklist' of sorts was shared by Travis on August 3, 2012, showcasing a few songs that had been made since meeting T.I. and Ye (the Instagram post was captioned "tracklist so far"). Most of the titles are the session folder names. Note that these are simply in alphabetical order and not sequenced. It's assumed that "Ah Sample", "Hitboy", and "Harmonies" are simply sessions with ideas and not proper songs.

albums.name: Owl Pharaoh
albums.description: Part of a tracklist that could be seen in a picture posted briefly to Instagram by Travis on February 24, 2013. Some guesses have to be made, as the beginning of the titles become progressively harder to read. Unlikely to be sequenced. There may be more tracks that can't be seen underneath; for example, "Bandz" is very likely to be on here, as are "MIA" and "Naked".

albums.name: Untitled Album [V1]
albums.description: While it wasn't officially announced until later, Travis was openly working on a studio album alongside 'Owl Pharaoh'; he and Pharaohxx both made references to an album in March 2013, and Pharaohxx said that was originally meant to release in September 2013. Known songs from different periods are: Travis stated that the instrumental for JAY-Z's "Somewhereinamerica" was intended for the project, and he also said that he wanted to put "Can't Look In My Eyes" on it after Cudi initially scrapped it. According to Pharaohxx, "Armageddon" was also being saved for the album.

albums.name: Owl Pharaoh
albums.description: Tracklist shared by Travis on May 18, 2013, three days before release. "Blocka La Flame" is missing, "Naked" is the uncut version, "Chazz Interlude" is a lot longer, "Dance on the Moon" is notably shorter and "Bandz" notably longer, and "Quintana" is solo. Most other tracks are at least a few seconds different in length to what was released, excluding "Quintana" (was released as a single prior, and also used for the video) and "16 Chapels" (same as the version released in 2012).

albums.description: Announced by Travis to be a mixed and mastered version of the project with additional tracks, verses, and features; was set to be released in June 2013. No confirmed tracklist ever surfaced and the release was eventually quietly cancelled - GOODMUSICINSIDER later stated that Epic Records "dropped the ball" with its release. Tracks set to appear according to Pharaohxx were: "Blame" with Mr Hudson is a rumoured song.

albums.name:
Untitled Album [V2]
(Fuego)
albums.description: During an interview on HOT97 on July 16, 2013, Travis officially announced that he was working on an album, set to be released in 2014. At the time of the announcement, Travis said that he had recently been working with Crada, so any songs made with him are likely in contention; "Naked" and "Can't Look In My Eyes" may have still been in consideration (assuming Cudi hadn't taken the latter back yet) but "Armageddon" likely wasn't. Pharaohxx also said that the Rick Rubin rework of "Naked" would make the album. An October 31, 2013, Rolling Stone article said that Travis was considering 'Fuego' as a title, but 'Rodeo' was eventually settled on (in March 2014 at the latest). The project continued to evolve until eventually all songs from this time had been cut.

albums.name: Rodeo
albums.description: By August 19, 2014, according to GOODMUSICINSIDER, 'Rodeo' already had features from James Blake, Justin Vernon of Bon Iver, and King Krule, as well as a song with PARTYNEXTDOOR and Young Thug that we now know is "Perfect" [V2]. Other probable songs include "Pray 4 Love" and "Love".

albums.name: Rodeo
albums.description: Travis played a few songs intended for 'Rodeo' at a Chicago meet-and-greet in March 2015. The songs played (in no particular order) were: "Dipped in Gold" may have just been played for fun; it's rumoured that Travis wanted to use the song, but it's thought that he never recorded anything. Other songs such as "3500", "90210", "Act 1 (Drown)", "Never Catch Me", "Poet and Parade", "Pray 4 Love", and "Wasted" (among others) all existed at the time, but it's not known if they were being considered.

albums.description: Tracklist sourced from a document titled "RODEO SONG STATUS", dated April 14, 2015. Text in red is edited in (excluding the header); the list originally said 'Mozzy' instead of 'Mazi', so that has been corrected, and Keef has been added as a feature to "Nightcrawler", since he recorded for it on the same day. It can't be seen in the picture, but a note beside "Only One" says: "TWO VERSIONS EXIST. ONE WITH BEGINNING LOOPED THROUGH AND ONE WITH OLD ENDING". It's unclear how exhaustive this tracklist is. Songs like "Oh My", "Never Catch Me", and "Pray 4 Love" all existed at the time and could reasonably be expected to appear, but they equally may not have been in consideration at this time; "Pray 4 Love" was handled entirely by The Weeknd's team, which could explain its absence.

albums.name: Rodeo [Considerations]

Not sequenced, it's simply a list of songs that could've been in consideration for 'Rodeo', with notes on the state of their completion and possible features (some hadn't recorded and didn't in the end). Note that "Ok Alright", "Maria I'm Drunk", and "Oh My Dis Side" existed at this point, but they were treated as individual songs on the list so that they could have their progression tracked more easily. albums.description: A list of songs from July 1, 2015, that were being actively worked on by Travis. Very close to completion at this point, but is still missing some songs and has more that were later cut. Note that "Ok Alright", "Maria I'm Drunk", and "Oh My Dis Side" existed at this point, but they were treated as individual songs on the list so that  they could have their progression tracked more easily. "20 Naked Bitches" is likely a feature rather than a 'Rodeo' consideration. This is the first time that "Twist One Up" and "Poet and Parade" had been revisited since the April 14 tracklist. It's unknown why "My Ex Best Friend" has such a confusing and unclear title. Click the link to see the full images.

albums.name: Rodeo
albums.description: Whiteboard tracklist shared by Mike Dean after the release of the album; Mike had previously shared a picture of the same whiteboard featuring only "3500" on July 13, 2015, and it appeared briefly in the back of a Snapchat video posted by Allen Ritter on July 21. Unlikely to be sequenced. Quite a few songs were still unfinished at this stage. "Impossible" and "Apple Pie" are missing; "Apple Pie" existed at the time, but it's not known if "Impossible" did. "Nightcrawler" is listed as "Night Call", which was its new title from June onwards; it was also titled this on the CD leak, though it was changed back to "Nightcrawler" for the official release. "Pray 4 Love" is listed as "Pray For Love". "My Ex Best Friend" has been crossed out, and a song has been erased. Possible contenders for the erased song are "Twist One Up" and "Poet and Parade" (which were both revisited and reconsidered for the album shortly before this tracklist was penned), and "Joyride" (which was sent to Rihanna around this time); the latter two are the only two songs that look like they could fit what is left of the erased text, but "Poet and Parade" is currently the most likely. The same tracklist was printed on merchandising tees for Rodeo's 10th anniversary in 2025.

albums.name: Rodeo [Final Version]
albums.description: Whiteboard tracklist shared by Mike Dean after the release of the album. ------------------------ Everything is identical other than a couple of track titles ("Pray 4 Love" as "Pray for Love", and "Nightcrawler" as "Night Call"). Reveals that "Flying High" was originally meant to be a bonus track on the deluxe edition.

albums.description: Travis has stated that 'Birds in the Trap Sing McKnight' was originally titled 'Tina', before Quavo's line from "Pick Up the Phone" inspired him to change it (this likely would've taken place in March 2016). "Goosebumps" was confirmed to be on it on .WAV Radio; basically any song created in the period between the release of 'Rodeo' and March 2016 could've been in contention at the time.

albums.era: Birds In The Trap Sing McKnight
albums.name: Birds In The Trap Sing McKnight
albums.description: Posted by Tom Kahre, an engineer who worked on the album, a couple of years after its release. Based on the present songs and the features that Travis said were going to be on the album in an August 12, 2016 episode of .WAV Radio, it can be presumed that the tracklist is from sometime in July-August. Two pieces of supporting evidence: 1) The original "Guidance" dropped June 5, 2016, so it can't have been before then; 2) "All I Know" was recorded in early July 2016, and Kamaiyah was still on the album as of August 12. "Late Nights" is "Through the Late Night"; "Outside" was possibly solo at this point, and "RaRa" may be too if it didn't feature Offset at this point. Differences for every other song are likely, but unknown.

albums.name: Astroworld [Final Version]
albums.description: Whiteboard tracklist shared by Mike Dean after the release of the album. No differences, other than "WAKE UP" being titled "DON'T WANNA WAKE UP". Reveals that "WHO? WHAT?" was a last-minute addition, though it was already known to be the last song recorded for the album, per the Complex cover. It also appears that there may have been a song at track 17 (now 18 after the inclusion of "WHO? WHAT?") that was scrapped very late on, as one of the columns has a check mark.  This song could possibly be "Watch" as it would fit as an outro, but the lack of check marks suggest that the song didn't get very far in the mixing / mastering stage, while "Watch" had already received the full Mike Dean treatment.

albums.name: DYSTOPIA
albums.description: Based on information from a producer that has worked extensively with Cactus Jack, as well as what can be inferred from comments made by Travis as part of the GQ Cover 'The Reemergence of Travis Scott', Travis intended to release a mixtape titled 'Dystopia' in late 2021 or very early 2022, followed by the album 'Utopia' in early 2022. While the producer should be a reliable source, they also claimed that they had production on both projects, but didn't appear on 'Utopia'; it's still possible that they were telling the truth and were simply cut. Regardless, the aforementioned GQ Cover states that Travis intended "other releases" after the "Escape Plan" / "Mafia" pack - quite possibly 'Dystopia' - but the AstroFest tragedy halted the plans. While no tracks are confirmed, some can be speculated on. "Heartbeat" would be a solid contender. KayCyy mentioned that it was intended to be the lead single for 'Utopia' before the leaks messed it up; it could be that he was partially correct, and the song was intended for 'Dystopia' instead. Snippets like "I Need You*" would also fit the supposed darker vibe that 'Dystopia' was rumoured to have. It could also be the case that several of the darker songs on 'Utopia' were repurposed from 'Dystopia'.

albums.name: UTOPIA
albums.description: According to Travis in the GQ Cover 'The Reemergence of Travis Scott', by the time that "Escape Plan" and "Mafia" were released on November 5, 2021, a version of 'Utopia' was roughly 50-60% completed. It can be deduced that a large number of the songs that made the final cut of the album existed at this time: -"Hyaena", "Sirens", "Delresto" were all verifiably started in 2020 -"Thank God" and "God's Country" were started by Ye in 2020; it's not precisely known when Travis took them. Studio images shared by KayCyy after 'Utopia' released suggest that "Thank God" was reworked in June 2021 -"Lost Forever" was recorded with Gunn in February 2021 -The first part of "Skitzo is from 2019. The second beat was added just weeks before release, although the later parts could've existed already -"Til Further Notice" was started in 2019 (technically 2018, by artist SwaVay), although it was a Metro song for sometime and it's not known precisely when Travis took it. -"Looove" was verifiably revisited in mid-2021 -The first part of "My Eyes" is said to be one of the first songs worked on the album according to Travis. -"Future Sounds" was started in 2019, with Travis recording in 2020 and the last version being dated just before the release of 'Donda'. It's not known when Travis took the song, but SZA (and probably Future) definitely wasn't on the song until very late. It's safer to guess it was reworked into "Telekinesis" by Travis after the tragedy -"Modern Jam" (atleast Teezo's recordings) seems to be from July 2021, although there's room for doubt Due to the lack of clarity surrounding the 'Dystopia' / 'Utopia' situation, it's difficult to speculate on what other songs were in consideration at this time and whether or not all of the aforementioned songs were intended for the album. "In My Head" is the only solid guess, since it was briefly previewed at Travis's Dior x Cactus Jack show alongside "Escape Plan" and "Lost Forever". "Respected" and "Hold On" are said to be from 2020, possibly meant for the album, but totally unconfirmed as of now. "Franchise" was first advertised as the opener of the 'Utopia' era in 2020, but it's likely it was later cut from the project in 2021.

albums.description: Some of the alleged considerations for 'JackBoys 2' in May 2025. The list is unordered. -"ILMB" was in consideration ever since June 2024. It was only temporarily removed in June 2025. -All of SoFaygo's contributions were chosen in April, although some of the songs had already been recorded. He might've also temporarily appeared on "Velour" too at this stage, but it's unconfirmed. -"Where Was You" was finalized in May, when Future recorded. -"Outside" was created in May, but YoungBoy was added later. -"Call Back" was played live by Don, who teased it as a 'JB2' song before the project's release. It was replaced by "No Comments". -"Bleed Out Music" is an early version of "K9". It was replaced by "Beep Beep". -"Satellites" is an early version of Chase B's "Satellite" and was in consideration in May; it's unknown exactly who would've made the final cut though. -Don's "FWU" might've been another contender since it was played live by Don, who labeled it as a 'JB2' song, before the project's release. -"Florida Flow" existed but was likely incomplete and it's unknown if it was in contention.
